chunks.text: This user requirement specification describes how Lakbay Freight's Transport Management System (TMS) sends customer billing to the ERP. There are two customizations: CR-01, where the TMS pushes invoices through a web service, and CR-02, where client companies that are not on the TMS upload a CSV file by hand.
chunks.embed:
Document: URS LKB-URS-007 v1.1 - TMS to ERP Billing Integration (client business process)
Section: Introduction

This user requirement specification describes how Lakbay Freight's Transport Management System (TMS) sends customer billing to the ERP. There are two customizations: CR-01, where the TMS pushes invoices through a web service, and CR-02, where client companies that are not on the TMS upload a CSV file by hand.

chunks.text:
1. The TMS sends billing data to the ERP through a web service.
2. The data lands in staging tables first.
3. The ERP creates a sales invoice from the staged data.
4. The created sales invoice is reviewed and manually posted by the billing team.

chunks.text: The ERP exposes a SOAP web service, TMSInvoice, that the TMS calls from its Billing screen with the Send to ERP button. One call can carry many invoices, each with many lines. The ERP stages the data, validates it and creates a draft sales invoice, returning the new document number in the same response.
chunks.embed:
Document: Technical Design Document - TMS Billing Integration (project document)
Section: Overview

The ERP exposes a SOAP web service, TMSInvoice, that the TMS calls from its Billing screen with the Send to ERP button. One call can carry many invoices, each with many lines. The ERP stages the data, validates it and creates a draft sales invoice, returning the new document number in the same response.

chunks.text: The TMS authenticates with OAuth 2.0 client credentials (service-to-service). It requests a token from the identity provider and sends it as a Bearer token with every call.
chunks.embed:
Document: Technical Design Document - TMS Billing Integration (project document)
Section: Authentication

The TMS authenticates with OAuth 2.0 client credentials (service-to-service). It requests a token from the identity provider and sends it as a Bearer token with every call.

chunks.text: The TMS sets IsFinalLine = true on the last line of each invoice and false on the others. When the final line arrives, the ERP knows the invoice is complete and creates the sales invoice immediately.
chunks.embed:
Document: Technical Design Document - TMS Billing Integration (project document)
Section: Completion Flag

The TMS sets IsFinalLine = true on the last line of each invoice and false on the others. When the final line arrives, the ERP knows the invoice is complete and creates the sales invoice immediately.

chunks.text: Every customer and item the TMS sends already exists in the ERP. Default dimensions and posting groups are set up on the customer and item cards. The TMS sends no dimensions.
chunks.embed:
Document: Technical Design Document - TMS Billing Integration (project document)
Section: Assumptions

Every customer and item the TMS sends already exists in the ERP. Default dimensions and posting groups are set up on the customer and item cards. The TMS sends no dimensions.

chunks.text: Invoices are created as drafts and never posted automatically. This keeps unvalidated external data out of the financial ledger until a person has reviewed it.
chunks.embed:
Document: Integration README - architecture and operations (project document)
Section: Why Drafts

Invoices are created as drafts and never posted automatically. This keeps unvalidated external data out of the financial ledger until a person has reviewed it.

chunks.text: The TMS sends the same entry number on every push, so lines cannot be matched to headers by that number. The header records a line watermark, and it owns only the lines inserted after that watermark.
chunks.embed:
Document: Integration README - architecture and operations (project document)
Section: Line Matching

The TMS sends the same entry number on every push, so lines cannot be matched to headers by that number. The header records a line watermark, and it owns only the lines inserted after that watermark.
